stories.title: Neo4j Context Engine Launches to Create AI Knowledge Layer and Enhance Agent Performance
stories.body: On October 20, 2026, Neo4j announced its Context Engine — a reusable, shared knowledge substrate that lets AI agents consistently reason over enterprise data across systems. The product includes a six-layer Business Ontology, MCP server integration, and a graph-native memory layer that gives agents short-term, long-term, and reasoning memory from past decisions. The launch reflects the August 2026 Gartner Market Overview for AI Context Platforms, which defines this category as software that constructs, governs, and delivers semantically organized knowledge to AI agents at enterprise scale.
stories.why: This is the architecture commitment a retail-AI seller can point to as proof: agents without a shared context layer hallucinate or contradict each other across merchandising, inventory, and service workflows. Neo4j's ontology-grounded approach mirrors exactly the 'context-before-agents' argument Graas makes — use this to show prospects why a data foundation must precede any agent rollout.

stories.title: McKinsey: 'Who Wins When AI Does the Shopping?' — Global Survey Shows 70% US Purchase-Completion Jump, Retailer AI Assistants Trail Stand-Alone Tools 2:1
stories.body: McKinsey's June 2026 Agentic Commerce Consumer Survey of ~21,000 consumers across 11 markets found the rate at which US AI users completed a purchase via AI jumped 70% year-over-year. Retailer-owned AI assistants trail stand-alone AI tools by as much as 2x throughout the shopping journey, closing the gap only at checkout. McKinsey also finds that for AI users, AI search is three times more influential than traditional search — a direct signal that brands not investing in agent-ready data infrastructure are already losing discovery-layer share.
stories.why: The 2:1 performance gap between retailer-built assistants and third-party agents is a live objection-handler: enterprises that try to build agent experiences on fragmented data lose to those grounded in governed context. Use this McKinsey finding to show CIOs that poor context — not model quality — explains why their own AI assistants underperform.

stories.title: Salesforce Acquires Cresta for Reported $2.7 Billion, Adding Voice Agents and Real-Time Conversation Intelligence to Service Cloud
stories.body: On November 2, 2026, Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta — the voice-first operating system for customer experience whose customers include Marriott, Comcast, and Alaska Airlines — for a reported $2.7 billion. Cresta had passed $100 million in ARR as of April 2026 and its platform combines end-to-end voice agents, real-time human-rep coaching, and conversation analytics on a single system. The deal is expected to close in Q1 of Salesforce's FY2028, and Cresta will continue supporting existing contact-center and telephony platforms post-close.
stories.why: Salesforce now bundles Fin (bought for ~$3.6B in June 2026) and Cresta (~$2.7B) into Agentforce and Service Cloud — meaning any enterprise on Salesforce CRM faces a default agent offering from the same vendor. Graas salespeople need to know this consolidation story cold: it reshapes the competitive map and raises the question of whether bundled-in agents grounded in CRM data alone can match the performance of a purpose-built, context-layer-first architecture.

stories.tag: US - analyst research / pilot failure rate
stories.title: McKinsey & Deloitte: 88% of Enterprises Use AI, But Fewer Than 10% Have Deployed Agentic AI at Functional Scale — 71% of Retail Merchants Report No Business Impact
stories.body: McKinsey data shows that while 88% of enterprises use AI in at least one function, fewer than 10% have deployed agentic AI at functional scale. Deloitte finds only 14% of organizations have solutions ready for deployment, while 42% are still developing their strategy. A separate McKinsey retail-specific study ('Merchants Unleashed', January 2026) found that 71% of merchants surveyed reported AI merchandising tools had limited to no effect on their business — identifying the gap between technology availability and effective implementation as the central problem.
stories.why: The 71% merchant failure rate and the sub-10% functional-scale deployment figure are the two most powerful numbers to open an enterprise discovery call with — they validate that the problem is not willingness to invest in AI but the absence of the data foundation that makes agents work. This is Graas's core positioning: pilots stall because context is missing, not because the model is wrong.

stories.tag: US/Global - named enterprise deployment / CPG supply chain
stories.title: BCG Report: Agentic Supply Chain AI Shifts CPG Replenishment from Periodic Planning to Daily Optimization — with Named Case Benchmarks
stories.body: BCG's 2026 Executive Perspectives report on supply chain AI documents a global CPG leader that redesigned replenishment using a modular agent back-end, shifting from periodic human-led planning to agent-facilitated daily inventory optimization at the most granular level to reduce out-of-stocks and increase sales. BCG frames this as agentic AI eliminating the historic tradeoff between effectiveness and efficiency — supply chains can now simultaneously optimize across SKUs with agents flagging shortfalls overnight and evaluating all options by 6 AM. The report identifies demand-supply balancing, inventory allocation from DC to store, and constrained-supply SKU allocation as the highest-value agent use cases in retail and CPG.
stories.why: This is a named-research proof point that agentic supply-chain outcomes are real and benchmarked — not vaporware. For Graas sellers calling on CPG and grocery, BCG's framing of 'daily granular optimization' maps directly to the ordering and replenishment workflows where a governed data layer is the prerequisite: without unified SKU and inventory context, agents cannot make the allocation decisions BCG describes.
